questions.question: At 10 billion transactions per day, what does a 0.8% false-positive rate imply for 9.9 billion legitimate transactions?
options: About 792,000 false alerts per day
About 7.92 million false alerts per day
About 79.2 million false alerts per day
Exactly 800 million false alerts per day
questions.explanation: 9.9 billion legitimate transactions multiplied by 0.008 equals 79.2 million. This is why the rate target cannot be used as the human-review capacity plan.

questions.question: Why should the decision service record one immutable release manifest ID?
options: It makes all payment retries produce a newly scored answer
It identifies the feature definitions, model, calibrator, thresholds, and rules needed to reproduce the action
It removes the need to retain reason codes or feature timestamps
It lets online services read every artifact from a mutable latest pointer
questions.explanation: A single manifest ties the decision to the complete versioned evidence and policy bundle, which supports audit, disputes, rollback, and reproducibility.

questions.question: Which training practice best prevents leakage from delayed chargeback labels?
options: Recompute every historical feature using the newest customer profile
Treat every transaction without an immediate chargeback as legitimate
Use matured cohorts and join only features known at the original transaction time
Train only on the highest model scores from the current release
questions.explanation: Matured cohorts allow the label window to close, while point-in-time joins prevent future outcomes from leaking into historical features.

questions.question: A higher automatic-block threshold usually creates which trade-off?
options: More legitimate blocks and higher fraud recall
Fewer legitimate blocks but more fraudulent transactions may escape automatic blocking
A larger review team without changing the queue
Perfect calibration for every merchant category
questions.explanation: Raising the threshold makes automatic blocking more selective. That normally reduces false blocks but also lowers recall unless another action band catches the missed fraud.

questions.question: What is the safest default when the model scorer times out but a versioned rules fallback is healthy?
options: Approve every payment so availability remains high
Block every payment until the model returns
Apply the rehearsed rules policy, record missing evidence, and reconcile eligible events later
Retry the model indefinitely inside the payment authorization request
questions.explanation: A bounded, versioned rules path preserves the deadline and auditability without turning one dependency failure into universal fraud exposure or customer denial.

questions.question: Which release result should block promotion even if aggregate fraud recall improves?
options: The challenger uses a smaller artifact than production
The model produces stable reason codes
A critical market slice doubles high-value false blocks and exceeds review capacity
Shadow traffic shows some expected disagreement with production
questions.explanation: Release gates must protect slice-level customer harm and operational capacity. An aggregate gain cannot compensate for a severe, user-visible regression.
